sanskrit: praviśya ca sa tāṃ senāṃ śalyaḥ parabalārdanaḥ nyayacchat turagān hṛṣṭo yatra yatraicchad agraṇīḥ
english: Plunging into that host, Śalya, crusher of hostile armies, joyfully reined the horses wherever their foremost driver wished to go.

sanskrit: taṃ rathaṃ meghasaṃkāśaṃ vaiyāghraparivāraṇam saṃdṛśya pāṇḍupāñcālās trastā āsan viśāṃ pate
english: At the sight of that chariot, dark as a thundercloud and draped with tiger-skins, the Pāṇḍavas and Pāñcālas were stricken with terror, O lord of peoples.

sanskrit: tato rathasya ninadaḥ prādurāsīn mahāraṇe parjanyasamanirghoṣaḥ parvatasyeva dīryataḥ
english: Then in that great battle the rumble of the chariot arose, loud as a rain-cloud, like the crash of a mountain splitting apart.

sanskrit: tataḥ śaraśatais tīkṣṇaiḥ karṇo 'py ākarṇaniḥsṛtaiḥ jaghāna pāṇḍavabalaṃ śataśo 'tha sahasraśaḥ
english: Then Karṇa too, with hundreds of keen shafts drawn back to the ear and let fly, slew the army of the Pāṇḍavas by hundreds and by thousands.

sanskrit: taṃ tathā samare karma kurvāṇam atimānuṣam parivavrur maheṣvāsāḥ pāṇḍavānāṃ mahārathāḥ
english: As he wrought that more-than-human work in the fray, the great bowmen and mighty car-warriors of the Pāṇḍavas encircled him.

sanskrit: taṃ śikhaṇḍī ca bhīmaś ca dhṛṣṭadyumnaś ca pārṣataḥ nakulaḥ sahadevaś ca draupadeyāḥ sasātyakāḥ parivavrur jighāṃsanto rādheyaṃ śaravṛṣṭibhiḥ
english: Śikhaṇḍin and Bhīma, Dhṛṣṭadyumna the son of Pṛṣata, Nakula and Sahadeva, the sons of Draupadī together with Sātyaki — all surrounded Rādheya, seeking to slay him with downpours of arrows.

sanskrit: sātyakis tu tataḥ karṇaṃ viṃśatyā niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ atāḍayad raṇe śūro jatrudeśe narottamaḥ
english: Then Sātyaki, that hero and best of men, struck Karṇa in the battle with twenty sharpened shafts upon the region of the collarbone.

sanskrit: śikhaṇḍī pañcaviṃśatyā dhṛṣṭadyumnaś ca pañcabhiḥ draupadeyāś catuḥṣaṣṭyā sahadevaś ca saptabhiḥ nakulaś ca śatenājau karṇaṃ vivyādha sāyakaiḥ
english: Śikhaṇḍin pierced Karṇa with twenty-five and Dhṛṣṭadyumna with five, the sons of Draupadī with sixty-four and Sahadeva with seven, and Nakula in the encounter pierced Karṇa with a hundred shafts.

sanskrit: bhīmasenas tu rādheyaṃ navatyā nataparvaṇām vivyādha samare kruddho jatrudeśe mahābalaḥ
english: And the mighty Bhīmasena, enraged in the battle, pierced Rādheya in the region of the collarbone with ninety straight-jointed arrows.

sanskrit: tataḥ prahasyādhirathir vikṣipan dhanur uttamam mumoca niśitān bāṇān pīḍayan sumahābalaḥ tān pratyavidhyad rādheyaḥ pañcabhiḥ pañcabhiḥ śaraiḥ
english: Then the son of Adhiratha, laughing, drew his excellent bow and, exceedingly strong, loosed keen arrows that pressed them hard; and Rādheya pierced each of them in turn with five arrows apiece.

sanskrit: sātyakes tu dhanuś chittvā dhvajaṃ ca puruṣarṣabhaḥ athainaṃ navabhir bāṇair ājaghāna stanāntare
english: And that bull among men, having cut down Sātyaki's bow and his banner, then smote him with nine arrows between the breasts.

sanskrit: bhīmasenas tu taṃ kruddho vivyādha triṃśatā śaraiḥ sārathiṃ ca tribhir bāṇair ājaghāna paraṃtapaḥ
english: But Bhīmasena, enraged, pierced him with thirty shafts, and that scorcher of foes struck his charioteer with three arrows.

sanskrit: virathān draupadeyāṃś ca cakāra puruṣarṣabhaḥ akṣṇor nimeṣamātreṇa tad adbhutam ivābhavat
english: And that bull among men robbed the sons of Draupadī of their chariots in the mere twinkling of an eye, and it seemed a marvel.

sanskrit: vimukhīkṛtya tān sarvāñ śaraiḥ saṃnataparvabhiḥ pāñcālān ahanac chūraś cedīnāṃ ca mahārathān
english: Having turned all of them aside with his straight-jointed shafts, the hero slew the Pāñcālas and the great car-warriors of the Cedis.

sanskrit: te vadhyamānāḥ samare cedimatsyā viśāṃ pate karṇam ekam abhidrutya śarasaṃghaiḥ samārdayan tāñ jaghāna śitair bāṇaiḥ sūtaputro mahārathaḥ
english: As they were being slaughtered in the battle, O lord of peoples, the Cedis and Matsyas rushed upon Karṇa alone and tormented him with masses of arrows; but the son of the charioteer, that great car-warrior, struck them down with sharpened shafts.

sanskrit: etad atyadbhutaṃ karṇe dṛṣṭavān asmi bhārata yad ekaḥ samare śūrān sūtaputraḥ pratāpavān
english: This most marvellous thing I beheld in Karṇa, O descendant of Bharata — that the valiant son of the charioteer, alone in battle, faced those heroes.

sanskrit: yatamānān paraṃ śaktyāyodhayat tāṃś ca dhanvinaḥ pāṇḍaveyān mahārāja śarair vāritavān raṇe
english: He gave battle to those bowmen who strove with their utmost might, and held back the Pāṇḍavas in the fray with his arrows, O great king.

sanskrit: tatra bhārata karṇasya lāghavena mahātmanaḥ tutuṣur devatāḥ sarvāḥ siddhāś ca paramarṣayaḥ
english: There at the deftness of the great-souled Karṇa, O descendant of Bharata, all the gods were pleased, and the Siddhas and the supreme seers.

sanskrit: apūjayan maheṣvāsā dhārtarāṣṭrā narottamam karṇaṃ rathavaraśreṣṭhaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ sarvadhanuṣmatām
english: The great bowmen, the followers of Dhṛtarāṣṭra's son, honoured that best of men, Karṇa, foremost among the finest of car-warriors, the foremost of all the wielders of the bow.

sanskrit: tataḥ karṇo mahārāja dadāha ripuvāhinīm kakṣam iddho yathā vahnir nidāghe jvalito mahān
english: Then Karṇa, O great king, consumed the host of his foes as a great fire, kindled in the summer heat, burns up the dry brushwood.

sanskrit: te vadhyamānāḥ karṇena pāṇḍaveyās tatas tataḥ prādravanta raṇe bhītāḥ karṇaṃ dṛṣṭvā mahābalam
english: Slaughtered by Karṇa, the Pāṇḍavas, terrified, fled this way and that across the battlefield at the sight of the mighty Karṇa.

sanskrit: tatrākrando mahān āsīt pāñcālānāṃ mahāraṇe vadhyatāṃ sāyakais tīkṣṇaiḥ karṇacāpavaracyutaiḥ
english: There arose a great wailing of the Pāñcālas in that mighty battle, as they were cut down by the keen shafts sped from Karṇa's excellent bow.

sanskrit: tena śabdena vitrastā pāṇḍavānāṃ mahācamūḥ karṇam ekaṃ raṇe yodhaṃ menire tatra śātravāḥ
english: Affrighted by that uproar, the great army of the Pāṇḍavas — those foes there in the battle — reckoned Karṇa to be the one fighter that was.

sanskrit: tatrādbhutaṃ paraṃ cakre rādheyaḥ śatrukarśanaḥ yad ekaṃ pāṇḍavāḥ sarve na śekur abhivīkṣitum
english: There Rādheya, harrier of foes, wrought a supreme marvel, in that all the Pāṇḍavas together were unable so much as to look upon him alone.

sanskrit: yathaughaḥ parvataśreṣṭham āsādyābhipradīryate tathā tat pāṇḍavaṃ sainyaṃ karṇam āsādya dīryate
english: As a flood, striking against the mightiest of mountains, is shattered and scattered, so that Pāṇḍava army, coming upon Karṇa, was broken asunder.

sanskrit: karṇo 'pi samare rājan vidhūmo 'gnir iva jvalan dahaṃs tasthau mahābāhuḥ pāṇḍavānāṃ mahācamūm
english: And Karṇa too, O king, blazing in the battle like a smokeless fire, the mighty-armed one, stood there consuming the great army of the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: śirāṃsi ca mahārāja karṇāṃś cañcalakuṇḍalān bāhūṃś ca vīro vīrāṇāṃ ciccheda laghu ceṣubhiḥ
english: And swiftly, O great king, the hero severed with his shafts the heads of heroes — together with their swaying earrings — their ears, and their arms.

sanskrit: hastidantān tsarūn khaḍgān dhvajāñ śaktīr hayān gajān rathāṃś ca vividhān rājan patākā vyajanāni ca
english: Elephants' tusks, hilts and swords, banners, lances, horses, elephants, and chariots of many kinds, O king, ensigns and fans —

sanskrit: akṣeṣāyugayoktrāṇi cakrāṇi vividhāni ca ciccheda śatadhā karṇo yodhavratam anuṣṭhitaḥ
english: axles, arrows, yokes and traces, and wheels of every kind — Karṇa cut them into a hundred pieces, keeping fast to the warrior's vow.

sanskrit: tatra bhārata karṇena nihatair gajavājibhiḥ agamyarūpā pṛthivī māṃsaśoṇitakardamā
english: There, O descendant of Bharata, with the elephants and horses slain by Karṇa, the earth became impassable, a mire of flesh and blood.

sanskrit: viṣamaṃ ca samaṃ caiva hatair aśvapadātibhiḥ rathaiś ca kuñjaraiś caiva na prājñāyata kiṃ cana
english: With slain horsemen and foot-soldiers, with chariots and elephants, neither rough ground nor level could be told apart — nothing whatever could be discerned.

sanskrit: nāpi sve na pare yodhāḥ prājñāyanta parasparam ghore śarāndhakāre tu karṇāstre ca vijṛmbhite
english: Neither one's own warriors nor the enemy's could be told from one another, in that dreadful darkness of arrows when Karṇa's weapon-storm had spread wide.

sanskrit: rādheyacāpanirmuktaiḥ śaraiḥ kāñcanabhūṣitaiḥ saṃchāditā mahārāja yatamānā mahārathāḥ
english: By the gold-decked arrows loosed from Rādheya's bow, O great king, the striving great car-warriors were wholly overspread.

sanskrit: te pāṇḍaveyāḥ samare karṇena sma punaḥ punaḥ abhajyanta mahārāja yatamānā mahārathāḥ
english: Those Pāṇḍavas, the great car-warriors, though they strove their hardest, were broken again and again by Karṇa in that battle, O great king.

sanskrit: mṛgasaṃghān yathā kruddhaḥ siṃho drāvayate vane karṇas tu samare yodhāṃs tatra tatra mahāyaśāḥ kālayām āsa tat sainyaṃ yathā paśugaṇān vṛkaḥ
english: As an enraged lion drives off herds of deer in the forest, so did the far-famed Karṇa scatter the warriors here and there in the battle, and harried that army as a wolf harries flocks of beasts.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā tu pāṇḍavīṃ senāṃ dhārtarāṣṭrāḥ parāṅmukhīm abhijagmur maheṣvāsā ruvanto bhairavān ravān
english: And seeing the Pāṇḍava army turn its back, the great bowmen of Dhṛtarāṣṭra's host charged forward, raising terrible roars.

sanskrit: duryodhano hi rājendra mudā paramayā yutaḥ vādayām āsa saṃhṛṣṭo nānāvādyāni sarvaśaḥ
english: For Duryodhana, O lord of kings, filled with the highest joy and exulting, had all manner of instruments sounded on every side.

sanskrit: pāñcālāpi maheṣvāsā bhagnā bhagnā narottamāḥ nyavartanta yathā śūrā mṛtyuṃ kṛtvā nivartanam
english: The Pāñcālas too, great bowmen and best of men, though broken again and again, turned back like heroes, making death itself their rallying-point.

sanskrit: tān nivṛttān raṇe śūrān rādheyaḥ śatrutāpanaḥ anekaśo mahārāja babhañja puruṣarṣabhaḥ
english: As those heroes returned to the battle, Rādheya, tormentor of foes, that bull among men, broke them many times over, O great king.

sanskrit: tatra bhārata karṇena pāñcālā viṃśatī rathāḥ nihatāḥ sādayaḥ krodhāc cedayaś ca paraḥśatāḥ
english: There, O descendant of Bharata, twenty car-warriors of the Pāñcālas were slain by Karṇa in his wrath, together with their horsemen, and more than a hundred of the Cedis.

sanskrit: kṛtvā śūnyān rathopasthān vājipṛṣṭhāṃś ca bhārata nirmanuṣyān gajaskandhān pādātāṃś caiva vidrutān
english: Having made empty the seats of the chariots and the backs of the horses, O descendant of Bharata, and the necks of the elephants bereft of men, and the foot-soldiers put to rout —

sanskrit: āditya iva madhyāhne durnirīkṣyaḥ paraṃtapaḥ kālāntakavapuḥ krūraḥ sūtaputraś cacāra ha
english: hard to gaze upon as the sun at noon, that scorcher of foes, the cruel son of the charioteer, ranged about wearing the form of Time the Ender.

sanskrit: evam etān mahārāja naravājirathadvipān hatvā tasthau maheṣvāsaḥ karṇo 'rigaṇasūdanaḥ
english: Thus, O great king, having slain those men and horses, chariots and elephants, the great bowman Karṇa, destroyer of hosts of foes, stood firm.

sanskrit: yathā bhūtagaṇān hatvā kālas tiṣṭhen mahābalaḥ tathā sa somakān hatvā tasthāv eko mahārathaḥ
english: As mighty Time, having destroyed the multitudes of creatures, stands alone, so did that great car-warrior, having slain the Somakas, stand there alone.

sanskrit: tatrādbhutam apaśyāma pāñcālānāṃ parākramam vadhyamānāpi karṇena nājahū raṇamūrdhani
english: There we beheld a marvel — the prowess of the Pāñcālas, who, though being slaughtered by Karṇa, did not forsake the forefront of the battle.

sanskrit: rājā duḥśāsanaś caiva kṛpaḥ śāradvatas tathā aśvatthāmā kṛtavarmā śakuniś cāpi saubalaḥ nyahanan pāṇḍavīṃ senāṃ śataśo 'tha sahasraśaḥ
english: The king Duryodhana and Duḥśāsana, and Kṛpa the son of Śaradvat, Aśvatthāman, Kṛtavarman, and Śakuni the son of Subala — they slew the Pāṇḍava army by hundreds and by thousands.

sanskrit: karṇaputrau ca rājendra bhrātarau satyavikramau anāśayetāṃ balinaḥ pāñcālān vai tatas tataḥ tatra yuddhaṃ tadā hy āsīt krūraṃ viśasanaṃ mahat
english: And the two sons of Karṇa, O lord of kings — brothers of true valour — destroyed the mighty Pāñcālas here and there; and the battle that raged there then was cruel, a great carnage.

sanskrit: tathaiva pāṇḍavāḥ śūrā dhṛṣṭadyumnaśikhaṇḍinau draupadeyāś ca saṃkruddhā abhyaghnaṃs tāvakaṃ balam
english: In like manner the heroic Pāṇḍavas, Dhṛṣṭadyumna and Śikhaṇḍin, and the sons of Draupadī, all enraged, smote down your army.

sanskrit: evam eṣa kṣayo vṛttaḥ pāṇḍavānāṃ tatas tataḥ tāvakānām api raṇe bhīmaṃ prāpya mahābalam
english: Thus did this destruction befall the Pāṇḍavas here and there, and yours likewise in the battle, when they came upon the mighty Bhīma.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca arjunas tu mahārāja kṛtvā sainyaṃ pṛthagvidham sūtaputraṃ susaṃrabdhaṃ dṛṣṭvā caiva mahāraṇe
english: Saṃjaya said: But Arjuna, O great king, having marshalled the army in its several divisions, and beholding the son of the charioteer raging furiously in that great battle —

sanskrit: śoṇitodāṃ mahīṃ kṛtvā māṃsamajjāsthivāhinīm vāsudevam idaṃ vākyam abravīt puruṣarṣabha
english: having made the earth a stream of blood, a river bearing flesh and marrow and bone — that bull among men spoke these words to Vāsudeva:

sanskrit: eṣa ketū raṇe kṛṣṇa sūtaputrasya dṛśyate bhīmasenādayaś caite yodhayanti mahārathān ete dravanti pāñcālāḥ karṇāt trastā janārdana
english: "Yonder, Kṛṣṇa, is seen in the battle the banner of the charioteer's son; and Bhīmasena and the rest there are giving battle to great car-warriors; and yonder the Pāñcālas flee, terrified of Karṇa, O Janārdana."

sanskrit: eṣa duryodhano rājā śvetacchatreṇa bhāsvatā karṇena bhagnān pāñcālān drāvayan bahu śobhate
english: "Yonder is King Duryodhana, beneath his gleaming white parasol, shining bright as he drives off the Pāñcālas already broken by Karṇa."

sanskrit: kṛpaś ca kṛtavarmā ca drauṇiś caiva mahābalaḥ ete rakṣanti rājānaṃ sūtaputreṇa rakṣitāḥ avadhyamānās te 'smābhir ghātayiṣyanti somakān
english: "Kṛpa and Kṛtavarman, and the mighty son of Droṇa — these guard the king, themselves guarded by the charioteer's son; and if not slain by us, they will destroy the Somakas."

sanskrit: eṣa śalyo rathopasthe raśmisaṃcārakovidaḥ sūtaputrarathaṃ kṛṣṇa vāhayan bahu śobhate
english: "Yonder Śalya, seated in the chariot, skilled in the handling of the reins, shines bright, O Kṛṣṇa, as he drives the chariot of the charioteer's son."

sanskrit: tatra me buddhir utpannā vāhayātra mahāratham nāhatvā samare karṇaṃ nivartiṣye kathaṃ cana
english: "There my resolve is fixed: drive this mighty chariot thither. Until I have slain Karṇa in the battle, I shall by no means turn back."

sanskrit: rādheyo 'py anyathā pārthān sṛñjayāṃś ca mahārathān niḥśeṣān samare kuryāt paśyator nau janārdana
english: "Else Rādheya will make an utter end, in the battle, of the sons of Pṛthā and the great car-warriors of the Sṛñjayas, while we two look on, O Janārdana."

sanskrit: tataḥ prāyād rathenāśu keśavas tava vāhinīm karṇaṃ prati maheṣvāsaṃ dvairathe savyasācinā
english: Then Keśava swiftly drove his chariot through your host toward the great bowman Karṇa, for a duel of chariots with Savyasācin.

sanskrit: prayātaś ca mahābāhuḥ pāṇḍavānujñayā hariḥ āśvāsayan rathenaiva pāṇḍusainyāni sarvaśaḥ
english: And mighty-armed Hari set forth, with the Pāṇḍava's assent, heartening the armies of the Pāṇḍavas everywhere with that very chariot.

sanskrit: rathaghoṣaḥ sa saṃgrāme pāṇḍaveyasya saṃbabhau vāsavāśanitulyasya mahaughasyeva māriṣa
english: The clamour of the Pāṇḍava's chariot resounded in the fray, O honoured one, like the thunderbolt of Vāsava, like a vast flood.

sanskrit: mahatā rathaghoṣeṇa pāṇḍavaḥ satyavikramaḥ abhyayād aprameyātmā vijayas tava vāhinīm
english: With the great din of his chariot, the Pāṇḍava of true valour, that immeasurable spirit Vijaya, advanced upon your host.

sanskrit: tam āyāntaṃ samīkṣyaiva śvetāśvaṃ kṛṣṇasārathim madrarājo 'bravīt karṇaṃ ketuṃ dṛṣṭvā mahātmanaḥ
english: Beholding him come on, the warrior of white steeds with Kṛṣṇa for his charioteer, the king of the Madras, seeing the banner of that great-souled one, spoke to Karṇa:

sanskrit: ayaṃ sa ratha āyāti śvetāśvaḥ kṛṣṇasārathiḥ nighnann amitrān samare yaṃ karṇa paripṛcchasi
english: "Yonder comes that chariot of white steeds, with Kṛṣṇa for charioteer, slaying foes in the battle — the one of whom, O Karṇa, you keep asking."

sanskrit: eṣa tiṣṭhati kaunteyaḥ saṃspṛśan gāṇḍivaṃ dhanuḥ taṃ haniṣyasi ced adya tan naḥ śreyo bhaviṣyati
english: "Here stands the son of Kuntī, his hand upon the Gāṇḍīva bow; if you can slay him this day, that will be our good fortune."

sanskrit: eṣā vidīryate senā dhārtarāṣṭrī samantataḥ arjunasya bhayāt tūrṇaṃ nighnataḥ śātravān bahūn
english: "Yonder the army of Dhṛtarāṣṭra's son is being shattered on every side, in swift terror of Arjuna as he slays a multitude of foes."

sanskrit: varjayan sarvasainyāni tvarate hi dhanaṃjayaḥ tvadartham iti manye 'haṃ yathāsyodīryate vapuḥ
english: "Passing by all the other troops, Dhanaṃjaya presses on in haste — for your sake, I think, judging by how his frame is roused."

sanskrit: na hy avasthāpyate pārtho yuyutsuḥ kena cit saha tvām ṛte krodhadīpto hi pīḍyamāne vṛkodare
english: "For the son of Pṛthā, blazing with wrath because Vṛkodara is hard pressed, will be stayed in his eagerness to fight with none but you."

sanskrit: virathaṃ dharmarājaṃ ca dṛṣṭvā sudṛḍhavikṣatam śikhaṇḍinaṃ sātyakiṃ ca dhṛṣṭadyumnaṃ ca pārṣatam
english: "Seeing the King of Righteousness deprived of his chariot and sorely wounded, and Śikhaṇḍin and Sātyaki, and Dhṛṣṭadyumna son of Pṛṣata —

sanskrit: draupadeyān yudhāmanyum uttamaujasam eva ca nakulaṃ sahadevaṃ ca bhrātarau dvau samīkṣya ca
english: the sons of Draupadī, Yudhāmanyu and Uttamaujas as well, and beholding his two brothers Nakula and Sahadeva —

sanskrit: sahasaikarathaḥ pārthas tvām abhyeti paraṃtapa krodharaktekṣaṇaḥ kruddho jighāṃsuḥ sarvadhanvinām
english: the son of Pṛthā comes at you all at once with a single chariot, O scorcher of foes, his eyes red with rage, wrathful, eager to slay the foremost of all bowmen."

sanskrit: tvarito 'bhipataty asmāṃs tyaktvā sainyāny asaṃśayam tvaṃ karṇa pratiyāhy enaṃ nāsty anyo hi dhanurdharaḥ
english: "In haste he falls upon us, leaving the troops aside, beyond doubt. Go forth against him, Karṇa, for there is no other bowman to match him."

sanskrit: na taṃ paśyāmi loke 'smiṃs tvatto 'py anyaṃ dhanurdharam arjunaṃ samare kruddhaṃ yo velām iva dhārayet
english: "In this world I see no bowman other than you who, like a shore against the sea, could hold back Arjuna enraged in battle."

sanskrit: na cāsya rakṣāṃ paśyāmi pṛṣṭhato na ca pārśvataḥ eka evābhiyāti tvāṃ paśya sāphalyam ātmanaḥ
english: "And I see no guard of his, neither at his rear nor at his flank; alone he comes against you — behold the fulfilment of your purpose."

sanskrit: tvaṃ hi kṛṣṇau raṇe śaktaḥ saṃsādhayitum āhave tavaiṣa bhāro rādheya pratyudyāhi dhanaṃjayam
english: "For you are able to overcome the two Kṛṣṇas in the fray. This is your charge, Rādheya: go forth to meet Dhanaṃjaya."

sanskrit: tvaṃ kṛto hy eva bhīṣmeṇa droṇadrauṇikṛpair api savyasācipratirathas taṃ nivartaya pāṇḍavam
english: "For by Bhīṣma, and by Droṇa, the son of Droṇa, and Kṛpa, you have indeed been made the match of Savyasācin — turn back that Pāṇḍava."

sanskrit: lelihānaṃ yathā sarpaṃ garjantam ṛṣabhaṃ yathā layasthitaṃ yathā vyāghraṃ jahi karṇa dhanaṃjayam
english: "Like a serpent darting its tongue, like a bellowing bull, like a tiger crouched to spring — strike down Dhanaṃjaya, O Karṇa."

sanskrit: ete dravanti samare dhārtarāṣṭrā mahārathāḥ arjunasya bhayāt tūrṇaṃ nirapekṣā janādhipāḥ
english: "Yonder the great car-warriors of Dhṛtarāṣṭra's host flee in the battle, those lords of men, in swift terror of Arjuna, heedless of all else."

sanskrit: dravatām atha teṣāṃ tu yudhi nānyo 'sti mānavaḥ bhayahā yo bhaved vīra tvām ṛte sūtanandana
english: "And of them, as they flee in the fight, there is no other man, O hero, who could dispel their fear save you, O joy of the charioteer's race."

sanskrit: ete tvāṃ kuravaḥ sarve dvīpam āsādya saṃyuge viṣṭhitāḥ puruṣavyāghra tvattaḥ śaraṇakāṅkṣiṇaḥ
english: "All these Kurus, having found in you their island in the battle, stand fast, O tiger among men, seeking refuge from you."

sanskrit: vaidehāmbaṣṭhakāmbojās tathā nagnajitas tvayā gāndhārāś ca yayā dhṛtyā jitāḥ saṃkhye sudurjayāḥ
english: "The Videhas, the Ambaṣṭhas, and the Kāmbojas, and likewise the Nagnajits, and the Gāndhāras, so hard to conquer, were vanquished by you in battle by that same firmness —"
